chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali from his father from Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man whose slave had run away from him: Is it permissible for him to free him as expiation for Dhihar? He said, 'There is no harm in it, as long as he does not know of his death.' Abu Hashim said, 'And Nasr ibn Amr al-Qummi asked me to ask him about that.'

key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it (permissible)

ai.seo_question: Can a man free his runaway slave as expiation for Dhihar?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that a runaway slave (*mubaq*) remains valid for Dhihar expiation as long as his death is not known, highlighting the principle that physical absence does not invalidate the slave's legal status for *kaffarah*. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on the continuity of ownership and eligibility despite temporary flight, provided no intervening event like death has occurred. The chain of transmission through Abu Hashim al-Ja'fari connects this specific legal nuance to the broader discourse on manumission in the Imami school.
